typical_topologies: in point-to-point connections, such as between routers or network interfaces, using a mode called Asynchronous
This means that the address field is not optional, even on point-to-point links where it is not needed to disambiguate

id_routing.description: Interconnect may append bits to AxID to identify the originating master; slave-side ID_WIDTH > master-side ID_WIDTH
id_routing.compliance_note: Returning ID is the WIDER value; routing strips appended bits before returning to the master

fields.topology_type: Point-to-point or multidrop bit-synchronous serial data link; bit-oriented framing with sequence-number-based reliable delivery and sliding-window flow control.

supported_topologies.name: Point-to-point ABM (most common)
supported_topologies.description: Two combined stations exchange data peer-to-peer; full-duplex; used by PPP, X.25 LAPB, ISDN LAPD, V.42 LAPM, Frame Relay LAPF.

supported_topologies.name: Point-to-point NRM/ARM
supported_topologies.description: One primary terminal + one secondary terminal; unbalanced; used in older wide-area deployments and modem-controlled links.

supported_topologies.name: Multidrop NRM (SDLC)
supported_topologies.description: One primary + multiple secondaries on a shared bus; primary polls each in turn using SDLC Go-Ahead bit or modern selective addressing.

supported_topologies.name: Loop topology (SDLC)
supported_topologies.description: Primary + secondaries arranged in a closed loop; messages relay via Go-Ahead bit; rarely used in modern deployments.

supported_topologies.name: Asynchronous serial (PPP-async)
supported_topologies.description: Point-to-point asynchronous RS-232 link with octet stuffing; PPP-async is the most prevalent example.

master_slave_role_summary.description: Originates commands; polls secondaries; owns initialization, error recovery, and disconnect (NRM/ARM).
Responds to commands from the primary; transmits only when polled (NRM) or at will (ARM); never owns disconnect.
Acts as both primary and secondary; used only in ABM (peer-to-peer).
Primary in NRM/ARM; either combined terminal in ABM.

fields.interconnect_role: There is no protocol-layer interconnect (no router or bridge). HDLC operates at the data link layer between two adjacent stations on a single physical link. Multi-hop routing is the responsibility of the network layer (X.25 PLP, IP, etc.) and is carried opaquely inside the HDLC Information field.

ordering_guarantees.single_link: Bits are transmitted in strict order; receiver reconstructs the bit stream and recovers the frame boundary via FLAG_HUNT.
ordering_guarantees.frame_level: N(S) provides per-frame ordering within a station's transmit stream; N(R) provides cumulative acknowledgement of received I-frames.
ordering_guarantees.delivery_mode: Reliable in-order delivery in NRM/ARM/ABM (sequence-number checking + retransmission); unreliable datagram delivery for UI/UIH (no sequence numbers).

fields.memory_vs_peripheral_regions: Not applicable — HDLC is wire-level. Per-controller transmit/receive FIFO/DMA, address-filter, and sequence-counter register maps live in the SoC integration spec.

slave_classification.addressable_target: Secondary in NRM/ARM (multidrop SDLC) or peer in ABM. Address field provides destination addressing on multidrop bus.
slave_classification.data_producer: Any operational station may transmit I-frames or UI/UIH datagrams; primary in NRM only transmits when initiating; secondary in NRM only transmits in response to poll.
slave_classification.data_consumer: Any station receives every frame on the wire and applies address-filter to determine if frame is for it.

default_signal_values_evidence_tables: Control field bit layout — normal 8-bit + extended 16-bit
U-frame binary encoding table — 32 possible M-bit combinations
FCS polynomial table — 16-bit CRC-CCITT default, 32-bit CRC-32 optional

multidrop_addressing_topology.addressing_mode: Address field carries secondary's address; 1 byte default (256 secondaries) or extended (multiple bytes, top-bit-0 means continue).
multidrop_addressing_topology.broadcast_address: Implementation-defined; SDLC commonly uses 0xFF as group/broadcast address.
multidrop_addressing_topology.primary_no_address: Primary terminal in NRM is NOT assigned an address — all commands come FROM primary TO secondary, and all responses come FROM secondary back; direction implicitly identifies primary.

loop_topology_sdlc.go_ahead_bit: In loop SDLC, a special Go-Ahead bit pattern (continuous 11111111) circulates around the loop; receiving Go-Ahead grants a secondary permission to transmit.
loop_topology_sdlc.primary_role: Primary launches the loop; secondaries relay frames they don't address themselves and append their own frames before relaying Go-Ahead.
